questions_and_answers.question_text: Where may a wèile phrase come in the sentence?
What three categories of meaning does wèile cover?
What is the common combination wèile yào?
Is wèile a synonym of yīnwei?
Which word should you use for "because"?
Write the Chinese for "I came only for his sake."
Write the Chinese for "He went to six bookstores in order to get this book."

answers.answer_text: Wèile mǎi zhèiběn shū, tā qùle liùge shūdiàn.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "In order to live independently, she left her parents very early."

answers.answer_text: Wèile néng dúlì shēnghuó, tā hěn zǎo jiù líkāi fùmǔ le.
"Generation" — a counter; also an era or historical period.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "All three generations live together so that they can take care of each other."

answers.answer_text: Wèile néng hùxiāng zhàogu, tāmen yìjiā sāndài zhù zài yìqǐ.

articles.text:
9. Wèile néng hùxiāng zhàogu,        All three generations live together so
   tāmen yìjiā sāndài zhù zài        that they can take care of each other.
   yìqǐ.

Notes on No. 9

wèile: "in order to, for the purpose of; for the sake of." A phrase with wèile may come at the VERY FRONT of the sentence or AFTER THE SUBJECT.

Tā wèile yào dào Zhōngguó qù     Because he wants to go to China to work,
gōngzuò, suǒyǐ xiànzài zài xué   he is studying Chinese now.
Zhōngwén ne.
Wèile kàn diànyǐng, tā méi qù    He didn't go to class so he could go
shàng kè.                        see a movie.

Wèile may also come after shi: Zhèijiàn shì dōu shi wèile ta.

This prepositional verb covers a range of meanings falling under (1) BENEFIT, (2) PURPOSE, or (3) MOTIVE.

BENEFIT, SAKE
Wǒ wèile tā cái láide.           I came only for his sake.
Wǒ wánquán shi wèile nǐ.         I am doing this entirely for your sake.

PURPOSE, GOAL
Wèile qián, tā shénme dōu        For money, he is liable to do anything.
zuòdechulai.
Wèile mǎi zhèiběn shū, tā qùle   He went to six bookstores in order to
liùge shūdiàn.                   get this book.
Wèile bǎochí niánqīng, tā yòng   She washes with milk to preserve her
niúnǎi xǐzǎo.                    youth.

Wèile yào is a common combination which often means the same as wèile:

Wèile yào niàn shū, wǒ zhèige    I'm not going out this Sunday so that
Xīngqītiān bù chūqu le.          I can study.
Wèile néng dúlì shēnghuó, tā     In order to live independently, she left
hěn zǎo jiù líkāi fùmǔ le.       her parents very early.

MOTIVE OR REASON
Wèile zhèijiàn shì, wǒ juéde     I feel very embarrassed about this
hěn bù hǎo yìsi.                 matter.
Wǒ jiù shi wèi(le) zhèijiàn shì  I have come precisely because of this
láide.                           matter.

Even though wèile is sometimes idiomatically translated as "because," it is still NOT completely a synonym of yīnwei. When you want to say "because," use YĪNWEI. When you want to say "for the sake of" or "for the purpose of," use WÈILE.
